about: Every safety clause (NEVER, must, DO NOT, unless explicitly requested and the like) in the OpenCode 1.18.31 tool text the OA plugin compacts, with the phrase compact-tools.js keeps it with. test/compact-tools.test.mjs holds the compact text to every phrase, and the list to every clause of the pinned tool text in opencode-1.18.31-tool/. Re-derive it on an OpenCode version bump.

clauses.original: You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
keeps: You must read the file first

clauses.original: When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + colon + space (e.g., `1: `). Everything after that space is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the oldString or newString.
keeps: keep the exact indentation after the `N: ` line prefix
never include the prefix

clauses.original: ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
keeps: never write new files unless required

clauses.original: Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
keeps: No emojis unless asked

clauses.original: If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
keeps: You must read an existing file first

clauses.original: ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
keeps: never write new files unless required

clauses.original: NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the User.
keeps: never create documentation files unless asked

clauses.original: Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.
keeps: No emojis unless asked

clauses.original: If you need to identify/count the number of matches within files, use the Bash tool with `rg` (ripgrep) directly. Do NOT use `grep`.
keeps: To count matches, run rg in the shell, never grep

clauses.original: The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
keeps: it must be full and valid

clauses.original: Mark `completed` only after the required work is actually done, including any required verification. Never based on intent.
keeps: only when done and verified, never on intent

clauses.original: IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.
keeps: Use the read, edit, write, glob and grep tools for files, not shell commands

clauses.original: Only commit, amend, push, or create PRs when explicitly requested.
keeps: Commit, amend, push or open PRs only when asked

clauses.original: Before committing, inspect `git status`, `git diff`, and `git log --oneline -10`; stage only intended files and never commit secrets.
keeps: never commit secrets

clauses.original: Do not update git config, skip hooks, use interactive `-i`, force-push, or create empty commits unless explicitly requested.
keeps: Do not update git config, skip hooks, use interactive -i, force-push or create empty commits unless asked

clauses.original: If a commit fails or hooks reject it, fix the issue and create a new commit; do not amend the failed commit.
keeps: make a new commit; do not amend the failed one

clauses.original: If the output exceeds ${limits.maxLines} lines or ${limits.maxBytes} bytes, it will be truncated and the full output will be written to a file. You can use Read with offset/limit to read specific sections or Grep to search the full content. Do NOT use \`head\`, \`tail\`, or other truncation commands to limit output; the full output will already be captured to a file for more precise searching.
keeps: do not trim it with head, tail or more

clauses.original: DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings)
keeps: do not separate commands with newlines

clauses.original: If the output exceeds ${limits.maxLines} lines or ${limits.maxBytes} bytes, it will be truncated and the full output will be written to a file. You can use Read with offset/limit to read specific sections or Grep to search the full content. Do NOT use \`Select-Object -First\`, \`Select-Object -Last\`, or other truncation commands to limit output; the full output will already be captured to a file for more precise searching.
keeps: do not trim it with head, tail or more

clauses.original: If the output exceeds ${limits.maxLines} lines or ${limits.maxBytes} bytes, it will be truncated and the full output will be written to a file. You can use Read with offset/limit to read specific sections or Grep to search the full content. Do NOT use \`more\` or other pagination commands to limit output; the full output will already be captured to a file for more precise searching.
